entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Li Ching-Yuen was a Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor who, according to his own account, lived to the age of 197, making him one of the longest-lived individuals in recorded history. Born in 1863 in the Shansi province of China, Li Ching-Yuen began his martial arts training at the age of six under the tutelage of a local Buddhist monk. His experiences during the Boxer Rebellion and the subsequent fall of the Qing dynasty had a profound impact on his worldview and life choices. Li Ching-Yuen's longevity has been extensively studied and documented, with many researchers attributing his remarkable longevity to his strict regimen of herbal remedies and martial arts training. Despite his fame in China, Li Ching-Yuen's life and legacy remain relatively unknown outside of Asia, making him a fascinating figure for historians and scholars of Eastern medicine and martial arts.

Li Ching-Yuen's life serves as a testament to the power of Eastern traditions in promoting longevity and well-being. His experiences during the early 20th century highlight the importance of resilience and adaptability in the face of rapid modernization and social change. Li Ching-Yuen's legacy continues to inspire new generations of martial artists, herbalists, and individuals seeking to optimize their health and well-being.

In 2012, at the age of 189, Li Ching-Yuen was officially recognized by the Guinness World Records as the oldest living person in the world, a title he held until his passing in 1933 at the age of 190. Despite his remarkable longevity, Li Ching-Yuen's life was cut short when he died of pneumonia on May 6, 1933, at his home in Yunnan province, China.
